sources.title: RIT CSCI-599 Computer Science Undergraduate Independent Study catalog description
sources.author: Rochester Institute of Technology
sources.content: Students work with a supervising faculty member on topics of mutual interest. A student works with a potential faculty sponsor to draft a proposal that describes what a student plans to do, what deliverables are expected, how the student's work will be evaluated, and how much credit will be assigned for successful completion of the work. The faculty sponsor proposes the grade, but before the grade is officially recorded, the student must submit a final report that summarizes what was actually accomplished. Enrollment in this course requires permission from the department offering the course. Typically Offered: Fall, Spring, Summer.

sources.title: ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
sources.author: Association for Computing Machinery
sources.content: The ACM Code directs computing professionals to contribute to society and human well-being. Computing professionals should avoid harm. They should be honest and trustworthy. They should be fair and take action not to discriminate. They should respect the work required to produce new ideas and creative works. They should respect privacy. They should honor confidentiality. Professionals should strive to achieve high quality in both processes and products. They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice. Robust security should be designed and implemented when appropriate. Ethical computing decisions identify stakeholders, foreseeable benefits and harms, uncertainty, alternatives, and obligations.

sources.title: ACM Publications Policies
sources.author: Association for Computing Machinery
sources.content: Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence. It cites prior work and identifies the contribution being reported. Methods should be described well enough for readers to evaluate the work. Results should be reported accurately rather than selected to create a misleading conclusion. Limitations and threats to validity should be made visible. Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification. Conflicts and relevant relationships should be disclosed according to publication policy. A research project narrows a question, reviews literature, defines a reproducible method, evaluates results, and communicates for the intended audience.
